description.en: From Zheng He's fleets to Dezhnev's strait: how in two centuries sailors linked every continent, and what it meant for the Americas.

text.en: Admiral Zheng He's fleet of hundreds of ships made seven voyages across the Indian Ocean, reaching Arabia and the East African coast. The expeditions displayed Ming power, but the court halted them after 1433.

The Tver merchant Afanasy Nikitin sailed down the Volga, crossed Persia and around 1469 reached India, where he spent almost three years, including in Bidar, capital of the Bahmani Sultanate. He died near Smolensk on the way home; his notes, A Journey Beyond Three Seas, are one of the first European accounts of India.

title.en: Dias rounds the Cape of Good Hope

text.en: The Portuguese expedition of Bartolomeu Dias was the first European voyage to round the southern tip of Africa and enter the Indian Ocean. It proved that a sea route to India around Africa was possible.

Christopher Columbus, sailing for Spain in search of a western route to Asia, landed on the Bahamian island of Guanahani on 12 October 1492. It began lasting contact between the Old and New Worlds, transforming both hemispheres.

Spain and Portugal divided the lands of the world, discovered and yet to be discovered, along a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands. That is why Brazil became Portuguese while the rest of Latin America became Spanish.

Vasco da Gama's Portuguese squadron sailed around Africa and reached Calicut on India's Malabar Coast. Opening the sea route to India launched direct European maritime trade with Asia and European colonial expansion.

Pedro Álvares Cabral's Portuguese fleet, bound for India, swung far to the west and reached the coast of Brazil. Cabral claimed the land for Portugal, beginning the colonisation of South America's largest country.

Ferdinand Magellan's Spanish expedition found a strait at the tip of South America and crossed the Pacific. Magellan was killed in the Philippines; the Victoria under Elcano completed the first circumnavigation in 1522.

After a long siege, Hernán Cortés's Spaniards and their Tlaxcalan allies took the Aztec capital, already ravaged by smallpox. The Aztec Empire fell, and Mexico City, capital of New Spain, rose on its ruins.

In late 1541 Francisco de Orellana's party split from Gonzalo Pizarro's expedition to look for food and could not return against the current. Over eight months the Spaniards drifted to the Atlantic, reaching it in August 1542, the first Europeans to do so.

title.en: Spanish Manila and the Manila galleons

text.en: Miguel López de Legazpi founded Spanish Manila. Galleons sailing between Manila and Acapulco carried American silver in exchange for Chinese silk and porcelain, linking Asia and the Americas by regular trade for the first time.

In 1606 the Dutch ship Duyfken under Willem Janszoon, searching for gold and spices south of New Guinea, sailed along the west coast of Cape York. It is the first documented European landing in Australia.

Dutch navigator Abel Tasman became the first European to reach Tasmania and the west coast of New Zealand. A clash with Māori in Golden Bay prevented a landing, but these southern lands first appeared on European maps.
In 1648 an expedition led by the Cossack Semyon Dezhnev and Fedot Popov rounded the north-eastern tip of Asia, sailing through the strait between Asia and America eighty years before Vitus Bering.

source: Steps assembled from the event records included in this atlas.
